accountDeletionPage.title: Account Deletion
accountDeletionPage.lead: This page explains how to delete your Protek account from inside the app and what happens to your data.
accountDeletionPage.deleteInsideTitle: Delete your account inside the app
deleteSteps: Open Protek and go to Settings (or Account).
accountDeletionPage.deleteInsideNote: Deletion happens immediately. If you’re asked to sign in again, it’s for security (recent login required).
deletedData: Your authentication record (email/username) is stored in Firebase Authentication.
Any app data tied only to your authentication record (if applicable).
accountDeletionPage.noEmail: No confirmation email is sent, but the app shows a confirmation state after deletion.
mayRemain: System logs or encrypted backups maintained by our infrastructure providers may persist for a limited period for security, fraud prevention, or legal compliance.
These are automatically purged on a rolling schedule (typically within 90 days) and are not used to recreate your account.
safety: All data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS/TLS).
We do not sell personal data.
If your child uses the app, we follow Google Play Families Policy requirements. No advertising IDs are used for children.
accountDeletionPage.withoutTitle: Delete data without deleting your account
withoutDeletion: If the app includes options like “Clear history” or “Reset progress,” you can use them without deleting the entire account.
Otherwise, contact us and we’ll help.

blogPage.heroLead: Falls aren’t minor incidents—they’re a global health challenge, and delayed response can turn a manageable situation into serious complications. Here’s the problem, and why speed matters.

problem.title: The problem
paragraphs: Globally, falls are a major public health problem. An estimated 684,000 fatal falls occur each year, making it the second leading cause of unintentional injury death after road traffic injuries.

Over 80% of fall-related fatalities occur in low- and middle-income countries, with regions of the Western Pacific and South‑East Asia accounting for 60% of these deaths. In all regions, death rates are highest among adults over the age of 60.
Though not fatal, approximately 37.3 million falls severe enough to require medical attention occur each year.

Globally, falls are responsible for over 38 million DALYs (disability-adjusted life years) lost each year, resulting in more years lived with disability than transport injury, drowning, burns, and poisoning combined.
People who fall and suffer disability—especially older adults—are at a major risk for long‑term care and institutionalization.

challenge.title: The challenge: falls among the elderly
intro: Falls are a leading cause of serious injury in older adults—often resulting in fractures, head trauma, or worse when medical help is delayed.
Many elderly individuals live alone, which can mean hours or even days without assistance. This not only endangers their health but causes constant anxiety for their families.

solution.title: The solution: Protek by AMB
points: Advanced fall detection: smart sensors detect abnormal movement patterns automatically—no wearables or buttons.
Instant alerts: real‑time notifications to family or caregivers via a dedicated app to ensure quick intervention.
Privacy first: no cameras or microphones—discreet, reliable sensing only.
Versatile design: easy installation in homes, hospitals, and care facilities without structural changes.
Smart app: alerts, activity reports, and weekly/monthly insights.

steps.body: Continuously analyzes movement patterns and detects falls in real time.

items: Emotional trauma and loss of independence

blogPage.closing: Protek is more than a device—it’s a commitment to dignity, safety, and peace of mind.

quickResponse.title: How does delayed response to falls affect health and life?
intro: Falls are a major health risk, especially for older adults. While they can happen to anyone, the elderly are particularly vulnerable to serious consequences if help is delayed.
According to the World Health Organization, 1 in 3 seniors experiences a fall annually—and half cannot get up without help. Delayed intervention can cause severe complications or even death.

sections.title: Health impacts of delayed response
items: Worsening physical injuries: minor injuries can become serious if not treated promptly.
Risks include hip fractures, internal bleeding, and head trauma—sometimes requiring surgery or causing long‑term damage.
Complications from prolonged immobility: severe dehydration, low blood pressure, muscle breakdown, blood clots, and pressure sores.

sections.title: Psychological & emotional effects
items: Depression, social withdrawal, and chronic anxiety

quickResponse.conclusion: Timely intervention after a fall is often the difference between recovery and life‑threatening complications. With smart technologies like Protek, families and caregivers can protect vulnerable loved ones day and night.

blogPage2.heroLead: The benefits of contactless technology in healthcare: a silent revolution transforming the future of medicine.

contactless.title: The benefits of contactless technology in healthcare
contactless.subtitle: A silent revolution transforming the future of medicine
intro: Contactless technology refers to intelligent systems that monitor a patient’s health using radar, sensors, or Wi‑Fi signals—without physical contact or cameras.
This innovation became particularly vital after the COVID‑19 pandemic, offering a safer and more efficient way to provide care.
contactless.benefitsTitle: Key benefits of contactless healthcare technology

benefits.title: Minimizing infection risk
benefits.body: In hospitals and care facilities, reducing direct contact is crucial. Contactless systems can monitor breathing, movement, and falls without physical interaction—significantly lowering the chance of cross‑infection.

benefits.title: Ensuring patient privacy
benefits.body: Unlike traditional camera‑based monitoring, contactless solutions—such as the Protek device—do not capture images and do not require the patient to wear any hardware. This enhances comfort and privacy, especially in sensitive environments like nursing homes.

benefits.title: 24/7 continuous monitoring
benefits.body: These systems provide real‑time insights (respiration rate, movement, fall detection), enabling timely response and reducing complications from delayed medical attention—especially when fast intervention matters.

benefits.title: Ideal for elderly & special needs individuals
benefits.body: No buttons to press, no devices to wear. The system operates silently and continuously—ideal for people with Alzheimer’s disease, mobility limitations, or cognitive impairments.

benefits.title: Supporting staff & reducing workload
benefits.body: Through smart automation, healthcare teams can reduce routine monitoring tasks and focus more on critical care—improving efficiency and reducing burnout.

contactless.closing: A life‑saving necessity, not a luxury. Contactless healthcare has evolved from a futuristic concept into a practical necessity. With advanced solutions like Protek, it’s now possible to deliver precise, private, proactive care—especially for vulnerable populations.
